label: def:octonion-algebra
title: The octonion algebra $\mathbb{O}$
html:
Definition. The octonion algebra \mathbb{O}

The octonion algebra \mathbb{O} is the 8-dimensional unital algebra with basis e_0, e_1, \dots, e_7, in which e_0 is the unit, each imaginary basis element squares to -1,

  e_i^2 = -1 \qquad (1 \le i \le 7),

and the imaginary units multiply by the cyclic rule

  e_i \, e_{i+1} = e_{i+3},
  \qquad
  e_{i+1} \, e_i = -e_{i+3},

with indices read modulo 7 on \{1, \dots, 7\}, extended to all of \mathbb{O} by bilinearity.

The algebra is alternative — every subalgebra generated by two elements is associative — but not associative: (e_1 e_2) e_4 = -e_1 (e_2 e_4). It carries the norm N(x) = \sum_i x_i^2, which is multiplicative, making \mathbb{O} a normed division algebra. Its automorphism group is the compact 14-dimensional exceptional Lie group G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}), equivalently \mathrm{Der}(\mathbb{O}) \cong \mathfrak{g}_2 [baez2002].

Convention. The sign rule above is the Baez convention [baez2002], matching the multiplication octMul fixed in the Lean sibling. The choice is not canonical: 480 distinct multiplication tables are compatible with e_0 = 1 and e_i^2 = -1, all isomorphic as algebras but differing in which triples are quaternionic. Any statement that names a specific e_i e_j = \pm e_k is convention-dependent and must carry this qualification; statements about \mathbb{O} up to isomorphism, including \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) = G_2, are not [albuquerque-majid1999].

Base ring. The Lean sibling realises the product over \mathbb{Q} in exact rational arithmetic. Nothing archimedean is required: the structure constants are integers, and the derivation count needs only \mathrm{char} \ne 2, 3.
